canaries.name: high_is_start
canaries.note: Presented as skipping the output's leading-zero scan because `high` already marks the first used digit; it marks one slot before it, so every output gains a leading '1' (and empty input encodes to "1").

canaries.name: masked_lookup
canaries.note: Folds the high-bit check into one masked table lookup; bytes >= 0x80 whose low 7 bits are a valid digit (for example UTF-8 continuation bytes of non-ASCII text) are now accepted as digits instead of rejected. Upstream tests only use ASCII.
edits: let mut c = B58_DIGITS_MAP[b58[i] as usize] as u64;
let mut c = B58_DIGITS_MAP[(b58[i] & 0x7f) as usize] as u64;

canaries.name: full_sweep
canaries.note: Presented as a branch-predictor-friendly loop condition; sweeps the whole output buffer for every input byte instead of stopping at the highest used digit. Output is identical, encode does more work.

candidates.name: encode_limbs
candidates.note: to_base58 converts four input bytes per pass into little-endian base-58^5 limbs held in u64 (every intermediate stays below 2^63), then expands each limb into five digits, instead of one byte per pass over a one-digit-per-byte buffer. Output is unchanged, including leading '1's and the empty input.
